title: SFT corpus v1: rules, workflow blocks, campaign claims and studio traces as chat examples
request: Extract cleaner and simpler data from the R&D outputs for fine-tuning a small language model on data science and ML engineering, and write an outside-reader review of the project with a roadmap for that model.
spec: build_sft_dataset.py turning the 22 rules, the 10 workflow blocks and the campaign's claim memory into chat-format question and answer pairs with provenance noise (git hashes, machine details) stripped, deduplicated and split into train and validation; the Research Studio's clean export adds planning, proposal, critique and lesson traces; DCLab_RD_Review_and_Roadmap.md as the plain-language review.
plan: Convert rules, workflow blocks and claims into chat examples; strip hashes and machine details; deduplicate; split.
Export the Studio's agent outputs as clean cards and SFT chat lines without dumping raw trial results or out-of-fold predictions into text.
Merge both corpora into one train and validation split.
Write the review and roadmap for a small model.

decisions.decision: Keep raw trial results and out-of-fold predictions out of the SFT text.
decisions.why: They are analysis artefacts, not reasoning to imitate, and they are large.

decisions.decision: Use both corpora: what DCLab found and how the agent plans and critiques.
decisions.why: One teaches the knowledge, the other the workflow behaviour.

change: cluad_initial_reports/ (later research/llm-fine-tuning/experiments/sft/) with build_sft_dataset.py, samples and the roadmap; dclab_rnd/agentic/clean_export.py; sft_out/ with a manifest.

measurements.name: corpus v1 build
measurements.gate: Deduplicated chat examples with a held-out validation share; no quality gate beyond stripping hashes and machine details.
measurements.result: First build 104 examples; final v1 141 examples (127 train, 14 validation): 50 from campaign claims, 22 rules, 22 rule diagnostics, 10 workflow blocks and 37 from Studio traces.
measurements.next: Fix examples that cite an experiment id without saying what was done (done in v3).
measurements.against_gate: There is no quality gate: the final build has 141 examples, 127 for training and 14 for validation, from 50 campaign claims, 22 rules, 22 rule diagnostics, 10 workflow blocks and 37 Studio traces.
limits: A validation share of 14 examples is too small to measure anything about a trained model.
Nothing held out whole sources; corpus v3 later did, because examples from one dataset are near-duplicates.
The claim examples cite experiment ids without saying what was done, so they teach recitation.
No model was trained or scored on it; the counts describe the corpus, not its value.

outcome: A first corpus and a roadmap for a small model. The owner later found that its claim examples teach recitation of experiment ids rather than reasoning; v3 replaced them (see RD-sft-v3).
lessons: An SFT example must carry the context its answer depends on; a model cannot reason from an id it has never seen explained.
risks: Questions that name an experiment id without its context, teaching the model to recite.
Provenance noise (hashes, machine details) leaking into the training text.
Raw trial results or out-of-fold predictions dumped into the text.
Near-duplicate examples on both sides of the split, so validation measures memory.
